goal: Move Watchdog from a feature-rich prototype into a secure, billable, supportable professional SaaS product.

readiness_score.summary: Watchdog now turns the validated 3.2M-row statewide MOD-IV source into a compact intelligence layer and delivers those municipal benchmarks inside the property report on demand. Every marker detail page now has a consistent plain-English explanation, interpretation guidance, professional relevance, limitations, refresh contract and linked evidence trail. The production architecture still avoids a paid multi-gigabyte database for the statewide snapshot. Major remaining launch gaps are paid lifecycle validation, production observability, backup/restore drills and full server-side Data Center value sheets.

phases.title: Trustworthy core
phases.focus: Mobile clarity, entitlement QA, error recovery, first-run onboarding and a reviewed source-monitor baseline.

phases.title: Paid launch readiness
phases.focus: Stripe test lifecycle, webhooks, plan enforcement, support/legal review and a staging release gate.

phases.title: Daily professional value
phases.focus: Change notifications, saved work, exports, source lineage and profession-first workflows.

phases.title: Team operating system
phases.focus: Organizations, seats, roles, jobs, reporting templates, usage controls and integrations.

phases.title: Resilient platform
phases.focus: Monitoring, incident practice, backups, security review, load testing and native companion delivery.

items.detail: Plan, profession and subscription state owned by the backend; client-side View As remains presentation only.

Authenticated Checkout and Customer Portal are live in Supabase and the live Pro/Pro+ recurring prices are verified. Checkout is fail-closed behind BILLING_CHECKOUT_ENABLED. Stripe currently has charges disabled pending its account supportability/Terms review; the Customer Portal also needs Dashboard activation before launch.

The Supabase Stripe webhook is deployed and verifies the raw signed request before syncing server-owned entitlements or writing its idempotency ledger. The live Stripe destination is registered but intentionally disabled until its signing secret is installed in Supabase and sandbox lifecycle validation passes.
Saved Data Center views now use ownership + Pro+ RLS; profile role/plan escalation is blocked and paid entitlement tables remain service-owned. Continue auditing every legacy customer table.
Log access decisions, exports, API actions, admin overrides and sensitive workflow events using service-owned writes.
All 721 cataloged markers now have developer-visible source/dependency, cadence, trigger and refresh rules; marker detail pages expose refresh contracts. Formula/input lineage continues to expand.

Six-hour publisher fingerprint monitoring is joined by a daily NJGIN contract check. The 2026 Data Factory baseline validates 3,208,097 MOD-IV rows across 21 counties and the live parcel service schema/count while preserving a review-first publication gate.

Official bulk MOD-IV ingestion now validates, checksums and privacy-normalizes all county partitions; live NJGIN access requests only an explicit property-data allow-list. Raw statewide work products remain out of Git and production publication requires explicit approval.

The 3,208,097-row 2026 MOD-IV baseline compiles offline into 24 proprietary professional signals for 564 municipalities, 21 counties and a statewide baseline. Aggregate output is under 2 MB; person-level fields and raw parcel rows are not shipped.

The secure non-exposed Supabase warehouse schema remains available when Watchdog needs selected row-level historical workloads. The full 2026 statewide MOD-IV copy is intentionally deferred because the compact compiler and live NJGIN lookup satisfy the current product architecture without forcing a database upgrade.
Capture frontend exceptions, Edge Function failures, source outages and slow requests with release/environment context.
Scheduled database backups plus documented, tested restore procedure for profiles, saved work, verification and billing metadata.

Watchdog Terms, Privacy and Data Methodology drafts cover subscriptions, public-source limits, derived intelligence, Daniel's Law handling and non-consumer-report use. Counsel review remains required before general paid launch.
Account page shows server plan/status/period and launches Stripe billing management plus Pro/Pro+ changes. Usage, seats and richer professional-profile controls remain next.
Pro/Pro+ pricing remains public as product marketing, but customer CTAs collect early-access interest and do not invoke checkout until paid enrollment is intentionally opened.
Pro+ can persist selected columns and filters to an RLS-protected server table. Named templates, sharing and server-side result sheets remain next.

The 721-marker catalog now has a live property-to-municipality provider for the 24 compiled MOD-IV intelligence signals, exposed lazily inside Home. Next: reuse the provider in full customizable property/town/county Data Center result sheets.

Every marker detail route now provides a plain-English explanation, reading guidance, method/formula, professional use, limitations, refresh cadence and linked authoritative source trail. Relevant independent professional references are labeled as context rather than as the source of Watchdog values.
Select markers and evidence to generate branded attorney, lender, broker, investor and client-safe reports.
Queue bulk enrichment, exports, scheduled monitoring and report generation with retry, progress and failure states.
Track property lookups, bulk rows, exports, API calls and scheduled jobs by plan; enforce limits server-side.
Scoped, revocable Pro+/Teams credentials, rate limits, event delivery logs and secret rotation.
Teams need owner/admin/member roles, invitations, shared workspaces, seat enforcement and organization billing.
Notify users when a tracked assessment, tax, permit, source, deadline or derived signal materially changes.
Ask role and workflow at signup, then configure Home, Data Center, templates and recommended markers around that profession.
One fast search across address, block/lot, municipality, marker, report, saved view and action.
WCAG-focused audit of focus states, dialogs, tables, color contrast, mobile navigation and dynamic content announcements.
Measure LCP/INP/CLS, module weight, map cost and API waterfalls; establish page-level budgets and regression checks.

GitHub Actions now enforces a static protected-route and entitlement contract on every pull request and main push. Next: staged browser smoke tests for login, plan gating, Home, Dashboard, Data Center and checkout.

A manual GitHub Action now tests anonymous protected-route redirects against a non-production hostname and refuses the production domain. Next: provision disposable Standard, Pro and Developer staging accounts for authenticated RLS and entitlement smoke tests.
Time-limited Pro trial, onboarding sequence, activation nudges, failed-payment recovery and cancellation feedback.
Measure signup → property added → professional tool used → report/export → trial → paid → retained, without exposing protected property data.
Support requests include page, release, anonymized request ID, source health and safe diagnostics so failures can be reproduced.
Source/API status, incident updates, postmortems and subscriber notifications for professional customers.
Review, formula versioning, professional validation, deprecation, backfill and change notices for proprietary metrics.
Seat quotes, invoicing path, W-9/security answers, organization terms and admin controls for brokerages and firms.
